# Termcp

> Termcp is an MCP server that installs other MCP servers. The model's tool list
> stays at exactly one tool (`term`), however many MCPs are mounted — locally, or
> on remote hosts reached over SSH. The agent can author a new MCP and install it
> itself. Writes and installs pass a human approval gate.

Canonical name: Termcp. Also written "Terminus MCP" (the tagline). Site:
https://termcp.org · Repo: https://github.com/open-mcp-ai/termcp · License: MIT.

## Facts

- One MCP tool is published: `term`. Extensions do not add tools to the tool list;
  they are driven through `term`'s directives. This is the design intent, not an
  implementation detail (see `internal/mcp/term_register.go`).
- Install:
  - `claude mcp add termcp -- npx -y @open-mcp-ai/termcp daemon stdio`
  - `go install github.com/open-mcp-ai/termcp@latest`
  - Docker image, or a single static binary from the releases page.
- Distribution: a single static binary, ~12MB (10+MB), no runtime dependencies.
  macOS / Linux / Windows, amd64 and arm64 (Apple Silicon, Windows ARM64). UPX
  compresses a build to roughly a third of its size — measured: a Windows v0.2.7
  build 11.8MB -> 3.4MB, a current dev Linux build 15.4MB -> 4.7MB. UPX support
  for signed macOS arm64 binaries is not guaranteed.
- Remote hosts need only SSH. Credentials (passwords, private keys, passphrases)
  live in the local Termcp instance and are never handed to the model.
- Extensions (`kind` = `mcp` | `skill` | `prompt` | `custom`) are pinned,
  capability-trimmed sessions kept warm and restarted automatically:
  - `mcp`: a stdio MCP server (`command` + `args`) or an HTTP/SSE endpoint (`url`,
    relayed in-process — no second binary on the target).
  - `skill`: a read-only window onto remote files, scoped by a `paths` whitelist.
  - `prompt`: an interactive terminal with operating instructions attached.
  - `target` is an ssh_config profile name, or `internal` for loopback. Mounting
    an MCP that runs on another machine is the same template with a different
    `target`.
- Extensions that dial the same host with the same whitelist share one connection,
  each driving its own shell channel.

## Boundaries — read before driving Termcp

- A call outside an extension's whitelist (`allow` / `paths`) is refused with a
  `forbidden` error. It is not transient: do not retry it and do not look for a
  way around it. If you need the capability, say so to the user.
- Creating or updating an extension changes what the agent can reach, so those
  actions pass through review mode: expect an HTTP 202 and wait for the human
  rather than retrying.
- Host writes (SSH profiles) are refused with 403 when the instance was started
  without `--mcp-manage-ssh-configs`. The switch cannot be turned on by a call.
- Never close, terminate or delete an extension's session: it is shared, and
  killing it takes down every extension served by that connection. Termcp
  restarts a dead extension on its own — take the fresh handle from a listing.
- Secrets (sudo passwords, MFA prompts, `[Y/n]` questions) are handed back to the
  human and stay inside the shell; they do not enter the model context.

## Command spelling varies by version

The extension surface was renamed between releases. On older builds it is reached
through the shared directives — `ls ext`, `create ext <name> --kind mcp ...`,
`edit ext <name>`. On current builds it is a directive of its own — `ext list`,
`ext create <name> --kind mcp ...`, `ext get <name>`, `ext delete <name>`. The
running instance is self-describing: an empty command returns the guide, `help`
returns the directive table, and `help ext` documents the extension layer. Read
that before composing commands; do not assume either spelling.
